prompt:
Normalize the contact record embedded in the user message. Emit exactly one JSON object with keys "name", "phone", "email", "company", "country" and no surrounding text. Start with five nulls and replace them only as instructed below. Non-null values are strings.

Read only the contact block, not the surrounding note. Split record lines into label and value at their label separator (colon, equals, or tab); punctuation inside a value stays part of that value. Labels can vary and lines can occur in any order. Trim values and reduce whitespace runs to a single space. Discard empty values and the placeholders -, --, n/a, na, none, unknown, ?, null, TBD regardless of case; an absent line supplies no value either.

Route before transforming: the country line supplies country. For other values, an @ identifies email even under the wrong label. A phone can also be under the wrong label: ignore initial tel: and a final extension marker (ext., ext, x, # or extension) followed by digits, then test for at least seven digits and no characters other than digits, spaces, +, -, parentheses, dots and slashes. Use the name and company labels for the remaining pair, reversing them when the name-line value ends with a legal suffix and the company-line value does not. For this test and suffix removal, use this case-insensitive list: AB, GmbH, AG, Ltd, Ltd., PLC, Inc, Inc., LLC, Corp, Corp., AS, ASA, Oy, Oyj, A/S, ApS, SA, SAS, B.V., N.V., S.p.A., Sp. z o.o., K.K., Pty Ltd, Ltda.

Resolve the country line to uppercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 from an English, Swedish or German name, an alpha-2 or alpha-3 code, or a common alias, ignoring case. UK and Great Britain mean GB; Holland means NL; USA and U.S.A. mean US; Türkiye means TR; Czech Republic means CZ.

Use the phone without its tel: prefix or extension. Decide whether it is international before stripping separators: ignore an opening parenthesis at the start and check for + or 00. If international, delete literal (0), delete spaces, dashes, dots, slashes and parentheses, and convert the initial 00 to + if present. Do not change its calling code to match the country. If and only if the country line is missing, empty or a placeholder, use that international calling code to fill country when it identifies exactly one country. Shared codes, including +1 and +7, do not fill it. If the phone is national, remove spaces, dashes, dots, slashes and parentheses, remove one initial trunk 0 if present, and attach + and the normalized country's calling code. A national phone without country remains null. A non-null phone is E.164, with + and digits only.

For the name, split at the first comma if present and put the portion after it before the portion before it. Remove leading honorifics Dr, Mr, Mrs, Ms, Mx and Prof, ignoring case and an optional dot. Uppercase the first character and lowercase the remainder of each part separated by spaces or hyphens, keeping the separators. Preserve Unicode letters and diacritics without transliterating. For the company, remove a trailing listed suffix along with an optional comma immediately before it. Uppercase the first character and lowercase the remainder of each space-separated word. For email, strip enclosing < > and the mailto: prefix, then lowercase the full address. Keep final strings trimmed with whitespace runs collapsed. Never use notes, signatures, email domains or company suffixes to fill or change any field. The unique international calling-code rule is the only exception to leaving missing fields null.
